status: FIXED 2026-09-05 — coordinator verified LayoutShell.css:74-78 (open grid 60px | 280px | 1fr | 0px, drawer in flow, canvas 800) and the drawerPinned retirement at LayoutShell.tsx:268; boards 199:2, 2162:11660 and 2162:11838 redrawn to 60 | 280 | 800 | 300. Two of the three transient boards had been cloned from 199:2 earlier the same day, propagating the defect, and the layer name had been defended as declared intent.
finding: The 'Drawer (transient)' mode is drawn on three boards including the default returning state, and no code path implements it — the drawer always pushes the canvas, so the default state's canvas is 800 in the product and 1080 on the board.
evidence: Boards drawing transient: 199:2 (Drawer 199:42 280x812 at x=60 with Canvas 199:70 1080x812 also at x=60 — overlapping, so the drawer floats), 2162:11660 (Drawer 2162:11736 / Canvas 2162:11664 1080, same x=60), 2162:11838 (Drawer 2162:11914 / Canvas 2162:11842 1080, same x=60). Code: `.ls-root` is `display:flex; flex-direction:row` and `.ls-panel` is `position:relative` with `width: var(--drawer-w, var(--bk-size-drawer))` (LeftSidebar.css:224-232) — always in flow; the shipping grid is `.layout-shell--has-sidebar.layout-shell--inspector-open { grid-template-columns: auto 0px 1fr var(--layout-inspector-width,300px) }` (LayoutShell.css:183-188), giving canvas 1440−60−280−300 = 800. Nothing in LayoutShell.tsx or LeftSidebar.tsx branches on a pinned/transient flag, and no board draws the transition between the two modes.
fix: Decide the one mode. If transient is intended, absolutely position `.ls-panel` over the canvas column and add the trigger (click-away / focus-loss) plus a board for the transition; if pinned is intended, rename 199:42, 2162:11736 and 2162:11914 to 'Drawer (pinned)' and redraw those three canvases at 800 at x=340.

finding: LayoutShell's drawerWidth prop and the --layout-drawer-width custom property it writes are dead in the shipping editor: nothing supplies the prop, and the only rule that reads the property can never match.
evidence: StudioPanels.tsx:419 forwards `drawerWidth={drawerWidth}` but StudioPanels' own `drawerWidth` (declared StudioPanels.tsx:93, destructured :176) has no caller — grep for `drawerWidth` across src and demo outside rail/LayoutShell and __tests__ returns only those three StudioPanels lines. LayoutShell.tsx:295-298 therefore never writes the property. The rules that consume it are `.layout-shell--drawer-open` (LayoutShell.css:73-96), and LayoutShell.tsx:280 only adds that class when `!slots.sidebar`, while production always renders LayoutShell.Sidebar (StudioPanels.tsx:429).
fix: Delete the drawerWidth prop from LayoutShellProps and StudioPanelsProps and the `--layout-drawer-width` fallbacks, leaving `.ls-panel`'s `--drawer-w`/`--bk-size-drawer` as the one width source.

finding: Four of LayoutShell's eight slots have no production caller, and as a result the shell's focus-visible rules are attached to elements that never render while the element that actually holds the rail and drawer has none.
evidence: StudioPanels.tsx:411-538 is the single LayoutShell caller and uses only Sidebar (:429), Canvas (:455), Inspector (:494) and FullPage (:519); LayoutShell.TopBar, .Rail, .Drawer and .Footer (LayoutShell.tsx:46-99,167-177) are unused — the real topbar and footer are AquibraStudio.tsx:489 and :712. LayoutShell.css:361-364 gives focus-visible outlines to `.layout-shell__rail` and `.layout-shell__drawer` (never rendered) alongside `__canvas` and `__inspector` (rendered); `.layout-shell__sidebar`, which contains `.ls-rail` and `.ls-panel`, has no focus rule.
fix: Delete the four unused slots and retarget the focus-visible rule at `.layout-shell__sidebar`, or move the topbar/footer into their slots so the landmarks and the CSS describe the same tree.

finding: The keyboard board's seven region badges do not sit where its own 1→7 sequence claims: the canvas carries no badge, the page-tab bar carries two stacked on top of each other, and the rail and drawer are numbered one step later than the code cycles them.
evidence: Board 58:2 is 1440x900 (Topbar 682:2632 1440x56 @0,0; Middle band 58:21 @0,56; Footer 58:196 @0,868; Drawer (pinned) 58:42 280x812; Page tabs 58:71 800x36; Inspector 58:98 300x812). Badge frames, measured relative to the board: F6 1 (58:201) @6,6 topbar; F6 3 (58:205) @6,62 rail; F6 4 (58:207) @66,62 drawer; F6 2 (58:203) @386,62 and F6 5 (58:209) @386,62 — identical coordinates, both on the page-tab bar; F6 6 (58:211) @1146,62 inspector; F6 7 (58:213) @6,874 footer. Code order (regionCycle.ts:12-20) is topbar, rail, drawer, page tabs, canvas, inspector, footer — which regionCycle.ts:2,11 attributes to this board.
fix: Move F6 2 (58:203) onto the rail, F6 3 (58:205) onto the drawer, F6 4 (58:207) onto the page-tab bar, and F6 5 (58:209) onto the canvas viewport, so the board reads the order the code implements.

finding: The board named 'F6 region cycle + focus outline' draws no focus outline on any of the seven regions, so the one keyboard affordance the shell has is invisible — F6 moves focus and nothing on screen says where it went.
evidence: Stroke census over every non-TEXT stroked node on 58:2: the only 2px #1A56DB (rgb 26,86,219) stroke is 58:89 'Hero — SELECTED' (680x250, canvas element selection, not keyboard focus); Topbar 682:2632, Drawer 58:42, Page tabs 58:71, Inspector 58:98 and Footer 58:196 carry only mixed #F3F4F6 hairlines, and the rail instance has none. fix: Draw the focus ring as a 2px --bk-accent inset outline on each of the seven region frames on 58:2 (one variant per region, or a single 'region focused' overlay), and publish it as a state so the other boards can reuse it. Code already has the rule at LayoutShell.css:361-364 but on the wrong elements — see SH-C-14.

finding: Every board labels the page-tab bar 'canvas column only · >1 page' and regionCycle documents it as dropping out on one-page sites, but the code hides it only when there are zero pages — so a one-page site shows the bar and keeps it in the F6 cycle.
evidence: PageTabBar.tsx:212 `if (!composer || pages.length === 0) return null;` — the sole visibility gate. Frame names carrying the >1 rule: 58:71, 199:71, 199:274, 66:73, 199:478, 200:71, 200:282, 66:294, 66:510, 66:709, 642:3765, 2162:11665, 2162:11843. regionCycle.ts:16 comments '4 page tabs (drops out on 1-page sites)'. Boards 65:2 and 65:412 draw no page-tab bar at all, a state the code cannot reach with a loaded project.
fix: Change the guard to `pages.length <= 1` so the bar, the boards and the regionCycle comment agree — or drop the '>1 page' clause from the thirteen frame names and the regionCycle comment.

finding: regionCycle's visibility test uses offsetParent, which stays non-null for every way the shell hides a region, so F6 lands on the closed inspector and — in fullpage mode — on three invisible regions while never reaching the only visible surface.
evidence: regionCycle.ts:22-24 `isVisible` returns `el.offsetParent !== null`, which is null only for display:none, position:fixed or detached nodes. The closed inspector keeps `.bdi-panel` mounted (StudioPanels.tsx:494-515 always renders ProInspector) in a 0px grid column (LayoutShell.css:183-188) with `transform: translateX(100%); opacity: 0` (LayoutShell.css:264-282) — never display:none. In fullpage mode LayoutShell.css:311-320 hides the drawer, canvas and inspector with `visibility:hidden; position:absolute; width:0; height:0`, which also leaves offsetParent set; the page-tab bar is inside that hidden canvas (StudioPanels.tsx:488). The FullPage slot itself — `role="region" aria-label="Full-page view"` (LayoutShell.tsx:154-163) — is not in REGION_SELECTORS at all, so Settings, Templates and History are unreachable by F6. regionCycle.ts:18 also claims the inspector 'drops out with no selection', which StudioPanels.tsx:421-424 explicitly decided against.
fix: Test real visibility (getClientRects().length && getComputedStyle(el).visibility !== 'hidden') instead of offsetParent, add `.layout-shell__fullpage` to REGION_SELECTORS, and correct the inspector comment at regionCycle.ts:18.

finding: View mode removes three of the seven regions and no board in the shell section draws it, so the shell's second region model — the one an invited viewer gets — is undesigned.
evidence: StudioPanels.tsx:418,424,428,493 drop the drawer, inspector and the whole LeftSidebar when `readOnlyView`; LayoutShell.css:70 `html.bk-read-only-view { --layout-rail-width: 0px; }`. regionCycle then yields four regions (topbar, page tabs, canvas, footer) instead of seven. Section 1776:8385's 33 children are the 15 numbered states, 4 non-state boards and 14 captions — none is a view-mode state. The nearest board, 813:4676 'S1.6 · viewer-editor-state · read-only-chrome', is marked SUPERSEDED 2026-08-28 and in any case draws a full rail (Active=Layers) and a Layers drawer, neither of which view mode renders.
fix: Add 'Shell state 16 · View mode' to section 1776:8385: no rail, no drawer, no inspector, canvas 1440, topbar trimmed to the viewer set, footer present — and give it its own F6 badge run of four.
